# Synthesis #555: GELU × RLCT L0 Draft\n# Date: 2026-10-23\n# Status: L0 — candidate exploration\n\n## Activation Function\nGELU(x) = x · Φ(x) = x · (1/2)(1 + erf(x/√2))\n\nwhere Φ is the standard Gaussian CDF and erf is the Gauss error function.\n\n## Singularity Structure\nGELU combines:\n- Polynomial zero from x (algebraic, x=0)\n- Transcendental saturation from erf(x/√2) (analytic, not algebraic)\n- Smooth (C∞) everywhere — unlike ReLU (C0 kink) or ELU (C1-not-C2)\n\nKey distinction from #350 SiLU: SiLU = x·σ(x) uses sigmoid (logistic transcendental), GELU uses erf (Gaussian error function transcendental). Different transcendental functions → different singularity classes in R_an,exp.\n\n## Claims\nC1 (PROVEN): GELU is R_an,exp-definable. erf is definable in the restricted log-exp-analytic category (composition of exp/log/integral operations within the o-minimal structure). GELU = x·Φ(x) is a product of polynomial and R_an,exp-definable → definable.\n\nC2 (CONJECTURAL): The zero locus Z(GELU) = {x=0} ∪ {erf(x/√2)=-1, x→-∞}. The algebraic zero at x=0 creates a simple normal-crossing-type singularity. The transcendental saturation tail (erf→-1) creates a non-algebraic fiber structure at infinity. Singular fibers near x=0 have higher multiplicity than ReLU due to the smooth crossing (GELU derivative is continuous, creating a higher-order contact).\n\nC3 (CONJECTURAL): The smoothness parameter (GELU vs ReLU vs SiLU) acts as a singularity-class selector. GELU's C∞ smoothness means the local RLCT λ near x=0 differs from ReLU (which has a C0 kink with known algebraic λ). The erf-based smooth crossing may give λ_GELU < λ_ReLU locally (smoother = lower multiplicity) but the transcendental tail adds a global contribution absent in ReLU.\n\nC4 (CONJECTURAL): Generalization bound for GELU networks: λ_GELU·log(n)/(2n) + O(1/√n) where λ_GELU depends on the erf transcendental singularity structure. Predicted: λ_GELU ≤ λ_ReLU (smooth crossing reduces local multiplicity) but with a transcendental correction term from the erf tail.\n\nC5 (CONJECTURAL): Phase transition: networks using GELU vs ReLU show different loss landscape geometry near singularities. GELU's smooth crossing eliminates the ReLU dead-zone kink singularity but introduces a diffuse transcendental singularity. Training dynamics (SGLD LLC) should show GELU has lower local LLC near x=0 but potentially non-trivial LLC contribution from the erf saturation region.\n\n## Key Novelty\nGELU's singularity is TRANSCENDENTAL via erf, distinct from:\n- #58 ReLU: pure algebraic (polynomial kink)\n- #350 SiLU: mixed algebraic-sigmoid (logistic transcendental)\n- #169 (cosine restart, NOT GELU — no overlap)\n- #353 ELU/SELU/Softplus: partial smoothing spectrum\n\nThe erf function's analytic properties (entire function, not algebraic, faster decay than sigmoid) create a unique singularity class in the R_an,exp framework.\n\n## Open Problems\n1. Exact RLCT of GELU near x=0 — does smooth crossing give λ=1/2 (simple) or higher?\n2. Transcendental tail contribution: how does erf's exponential decay at -∞ affect global RLCT?\n3. GELU vs SiLU RLCT comparison — same local λ or different?\n4. GELU tanh approximation: does GELU(tanh) change the singularity class?\n5. Depth-dependent RLCT for GELU networks\n6. Fisher information matrix rank at GELU singularities\n7.
